an3.84:1.3: The count of “over a hundred and fifty rules” is found also at [an3.86:1.1](), [an3.87:1.1](), and [an3.88:1.1](). There are nearly a dozen extant _pātimokkhas_ in different schools and languages, all of which have a similar number and content of rules except for the final section, the “Trainings” (_sekhiyas_), which deal with matters of etiquette and have no special penalty when broken. Now, if we take the 227 rules of the Pali _pātimokkha_ and subtract the 75 _sekhiyas_ we are left with 152, thus agreeing with the count given here. It’s likely, then, that the _sekhiyas_  were not included in the earliest recitation. The list of _sekhiyas_ must have been compiled from niceties of etiquette mentioned in the Suttas and Vinaya (eg. [sn11.9:1.5](), [sn35.133:2.7]()), with guidelines developed in monastic communities added over time. | The recitation was on the _uposatha_ ([an3.70:1.5]()).
an3.84:1.5: The Buddha does not criticize the monk, who has admitted his failing honestly. Rather, he immediately looks for a way forward that supports him with dignity.
